run_metadata.coverage_summary: Swept all nine Tier-1 government portals (AusTender, buy.nsw/NSW eTendering, Buying for Victoria, QTenders/Queensland Supplier Portal, Tenders WA, SA Tenders and Contracts, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL, ACT Tenders) plus VendorPanel Public Tenders and the mandatory Tier-3 corporate channel (SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery) via web search. Tier-2 was sampled across GBE/water utilities (Sydney/Melbourne/SA/WaterNSW/Water Corporation WA/Greater Western Water), councils on VendorPanel, and a NSW GBE (Bradfield Development Authority). Nine genuinely new opportunities were grounded to buyer-originated portals this run: two Bradfield Development Authority AMRF supplier panels (Bundle 25 Raw Materials, Bundle 26 Manufacturing Tooling; both EOI, closing 31-Aug-2026), two ACT Government tenders (GovAI Chat WCAG Accessibility Testing, closing 17-Aug; Graduate Relocation Services, closing 11-Aug), an NT QTOL supply tender (PM044 Product Bagging, Nolans Project, closing 8-Aug), two Transport for NSW items on NSW eTendering (Hume Motorway litter/debris collection, closing 31-Aug; Jervis Bay Road Intersection Aboriginal artwork, closing 19-Aug), a NSW council RFQ on VendorPanel (Cootamundra-Gundagai stump grinding, RFQ2026/44), and one Tier-3 buyer-originated upcoming-tender notice on SAP Ariba (Energy Queensland vans interior fit-out, SR26889514). One still-open prior Commonwealth/NSW item (HealthShare NSW natural gas RFT, closing 13-Aug) was re-confirmed active. One genuinely new buyer-originated source was discovered: the Suburban Rail Loop Authority (SRLA) buyer profile on Buying for Victoria. As in every recent run, direct page fetching was blocked environment-wide: every government portal and every detail page (AusTender, buy.nsw, Tenders Tasmania, buy.nsw opportunity pages) returned HTTP 403 to the non-browser client, so all opportunity detail below is captured from public search-index snippets at headline level, not from buyers' own detail pages or tender documents.
gaps: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 (Forbidden) for every buyer detail page attempted this run, including AusTender ATM pages (e.g. https://www.tenders.gov.au/Atm/Show/2701a39f-879e-4e91-a49f-f5cccbacd3c4), buy.nsw opportunity pages (e.g. https://buy.nsw.gov.au/prcOpportunity/3AB3D56D-B5DE-47D7-8FAB389B81CF1B2F) and Tenders Tasmania's Open For Bids list. Portals continue to enforce anti-bot protection against non-browser clients in this environment, so full deliverables/requirements/eligibility/evaluation-criteria/contact/document extraction from buyer detail pages was not possible. All tender detail below is from public search-index snippets and is headline-level / pending verification.

Buying for Victoria, QTenders (QLD)/Queensland Supplier Portal, Tenders WA, SA Tenders and Contracts and Tenders Tasmania were reachable only via search-index summaries; no new jurisdiction-specific opportunities could be grounded to a specific tender ID + closing date beyond items already recorded in prior runs. A Tenders WA planned outage was again flagged for Wed 5 Aug 2026 17:00-19:00.

A 'Defence Psychosocial Risk Management Solution' item (closing ~16-Aug-2026) surfaced in an NT QTOL-tagged search result, but its subject matter (replacing/enhancing Australian Defence psychosocial risk-management tooling) is inconsistent with an NT Territory portal and is more likely a Commonwealth approach mis-attributed by the search index. It could not be grounded to a confirmed source portal or tender ID, so it was NOT recorded as a tender to avoid mis-attribution.

VendorPanel Public Tenders individual RFQ detail (e.g. Cootamundra-Gundagai RFQ2026/44) remains behind supplier login; only the public listing summary was visible, so scope, evaluation criteria, documents and contact could not be extracted.

Tier-3 (SAP Ariba Discovery, BHP, Rio Tinto, Woolworths, Coles, Qantas, banks, telcos, energy retailers): apart from the publicly-visible Energy Queensland upcoming-tender notice (SR26889514, an Ariba event that is registration-gated for full detail), no publicly-visible open corporate RFx surfaced without login. These channels remain registration-gated (Ariba/Coupa/RangeMe) or invitation-only; per spec the portals are recorded in discovered_sources and no corporate opportunities were invented.
Invitation-only management-consultancy RFPs (Accenture/KPMG/Deloitte-style) are out of scope by definition (never published) and were not sought as tenders.
recommended_seed_additions: Suburban Rail Loop Authority (SRLA) — buyer profile on Buying for Victoria (https://www.tenders.vic.gov.au/, buyerId 698214) plus procurement landing page https://bigbuild.vic.gov.au/about/about-the-suburban-rail-loop-authority/srla-governance/procurement-at-srla . Major Victorian rail-infrastructure buyer publishing supply/manufacture/sub-contract packages (signalling, station fit-outs, tunnelling, line-wide, rolling stock, O&M); buyer-originated, not previously in the known-source list.

Energy Queensland (EQL) SAP Ariba upcoming-tender notices — publicly-visible pre-market notices (e.g. SR-numbered events) are a useful early-warning signal for a known GBE already tracked; worth monitoring the public Ariba notice stream, not only the registration-gated event board.

tenders.source_name: Bradfield Development Authority — Industry & procurement opportunities (buy.nsw)
tenders.title: Bundle 25 — Raw Materials Panel for the Advanced Manufacturing Research Facility (AMRF)
tenders.buyer: Bradfield Development Authority (Advanced Manufacturing Research Facility)
tenders.description: Bradfield Development Authority is seeking expressions of interest from suppliers to be evaluated for inclusion on a Raw Materials Procurement Panel for the Advanced Manufacturing Research Facility (AMRF) at Bradfield. Successful applicants become qualified vendors supplying raw materials for the AMRF's manufacturing equipment.
tenders.deliverables_summary: Establishment of a supplier panel for the ongoing supply of raw materials to the AMRF's advanced-manufacturing equipment, to build a robust supply chain for a world-class advanced manufacturing facility. Full category coverage, volumes and commercial terms are set out in the buy.nsw opportunity documents, which were not accessible in this environment (HTTP 403).
tenders.eligibility: Open to raw-materials suppliers seeking qualified-vendor status; successful applicants placed on a panel.
tenders.contract_term: Two-year panel with an option to extend for a third year
tenders.submission_method: Submit by email to procurementpanels@amrf.sydney (per the notice, the buy.nsw portal inbox is not monitored for this EOI; submissions must be emailed)
tenders.delivery_location: Advanced Manufacturing Research Facility, Bradfield, NSW
tenders.reasoning: Discovered via buy.nsw / Bradfield Development Authority industry-opportunities search; grounded to the buyer-originated buy.nsw opportunity page (ref WPCA-AMRF-23-048). Genuinely new to this routine (not present in prior aggregate). Bradfield Development Authority is an existing known source.
tenders.notes: Headline-level. Reference, EOI type, closing date/time (31-Aug-2026 3:00pm), two-year+one-year panel term and the updated email lodgement address (procurementpanels@amrf.sydney) are from the buy.nsw / Bradfield search index; the buy.nsw opportunity detail page returned HTTP 403 in this environment, so specific raw-material categories, volumes, mandatory conditions, evaluation criteria and documents remain to be extracted in an authenticated/browser run.

discovered_sources.source_name: Suburban Rail Loop Authority (SRLA) — buyer profile on Buying for Victoria
discovered_sources.how_discovered: Searched for major Australian rail-infrastructure buyers and their procurement portals. The Suburban Rail Loop Authority (SRLA) is a Victorian statutory authority (operating under the VGPB) that publishes supply, manufacture and sub-contract work packages (signalling, station fit-outs, tunnelling, line-wide, rolling stock, and operations & maintenance) for the SRL East project, with a dedicated buyer profile on Buying for Victoria and a procurement page at bigbuild.vic.gov.au. Buyer-originated, not an aggregator.
discovered_sources.notes: New to this routine. Complements the already-known Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority (VIDA) and Development Victoria profiles. SRLA is obliged to publish a 12-24 month forward procurement summary; monitor both its Buying for Victoria buyer profile and the bigbuild.vic.gov.au procurement-at-SRLA page. Major head-contract packages are typically let to Tier-1 builders, so sub-contract/supply packages are the more accessible opportunities for most suppliers.

discovered_sources.source_name: SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery
discovered_sources.how_discovered: Checked each run as the mandatory Tier-3 corporate channel — the public posting board where buyers post open RFx. This run a publicly-visible Australian upcoming-tender notice surfaced (Energy Queensland SR26889514, van interior body/accessories manufacture and fit-out); full event detail requires a free supplier account (registration-gated).
discovered_sources.notes: Known source, re-verified to document Tier-3 coverage. Corporate and GBE events on Ariba (and buyer instances such as Energy Queensland, Transgrid iBuy, Western Power, NBN Co, Woolworths, Coles) remain registration- or invitation-gated; recorded as portals, with only publicly-visible notices captured as opportunities and never fabricated. An authenticated run is required to read individual event detail.
